long_biography.plain_text:
McLaren shareholder Mansour Ojjeh committed TAG funds to finance Porsche's development of a turbo engine for the team. The partnership helped Niki Lauda and Alain Prost win three consecutive drivers' championships. His ambitions extended beyond racing: he pressed for the creation of the McLaren F1 road car and later supported the establishment of McLaren Automotive.

Ojjeh left daily management to executives while remaining involved in strategic decisions, including the choice of engine partners. He expected to understand each business well enough to judge its management, but gave managers authority to run it. He also took a personal role in difficult staff decisions, joining Zak Brown when they told driver Stoffel Vandoorne that his contract would not be renewed.

He also took a personal role in difficult staff decisions, joining Zak Brown when they told driver Stoffel Vandoorne that his contract would not be renewed.

uncertainties.topic: Terminal personal assets and economic materiality
uncertainties.detail: All current fields refer to his lifetime ending 6 June 2021. The retained TAG McLaren stake is substantial, and operating accounts establish its automotive core. Corporate stake percentages and entire family trust assets are not assigned wholly to Mansour. Cash proceeds and other personal or family assets could change relative portfolio weights; Automotive is an explicit medium-confidence principal-asset inference, not a balance-sheet assertion. Known disposed aviation and watch operations are excluded. Original Service differs from retained Automotive; origin-sector fallback was tested but not needed.

The father-created platform, family-benefit trust and succession to control supply positive transfer premises. The precise individual allocation and timing of vested beneficial rights remain unresolved. Marriage / family transfer is the least-specific supported mechanism, without inventing marriage as the route. Continued growth within those assets does not establish a separate self-made fortune. Family office principal describes sustained capital direction, acquisitions and disposals rather than daily operation; directorship ended in 2020 but strategic involvement continued.

The source mortality value Alive is superseded by well-corroborated death on 6 June 2021. Birth date and French secondary nationality are supported independently. Paris is reported in credible obituaries, Saudi Arabia appears in the immutable input, and reference accounts also differ. No birthplace or birth-country correction passes the import threshold. Geneva residence context is insufficiently precise for a terminal main-residence proposal; the blank is preserved. System-derived ages remain untouched.

Forbes was checked first: coverage found, no exact personal profile. LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube, TikTok, Personal Website, Wikipedia and Company Website were checked, along with Vimeo, Flickr, Trip Advisor and Zillow. Results were company accounts, tribute posts, photographs, fan coverage, relatives or uncorroborated namesakes. TikTok restricts automated access. No personal account passes identity verification. Only the exact Wikipedia page and official McLaren company website are proposed. The sold aviation company and unrelated TAG businesses are not used as his current company link.

The McLaren-authored obituary was fully read on an alumni-site reprint because the original endpoint failed. The 2020 company report was read on a public mirror. DOT ownership and nationality passages and the relevant Forbes and Le Monde passages were read as indexed substantive bodies; direct access limitations are disclosed rather than represented as complete document reads. Regulatory evidence identifies collective trust benefit and trustees, not Mansour as sole beneficial owner. Family disputes, health information and speculative net worth estimates are unnecessary and omitted.

Motorsport and Watchmaking cover two distinct, materially documented activities. Both are former but defining. Motorsport is justified by durable substantial shareholding and strategic participation, not sponsorship alone. Watchmaking follows a substantial acquisition and fourteen-year business development mandate. Generic investment, wealth and collector labels are omitted; no taxonomy candidates are created.
